UpdateWorkflowExecution.trigger: After test client submits the Update RPC; allocate invocation slot and requested wait stage before History handles it.

UpdaterApplyRequestNew.trigger: After FindOrCreate + Admit with Immediate effects; before deciding/scheduling a new WFT, with lease held.

AddWorkflowTaskScheduledEvent.trigger: After creating speculative WFT and installing its STS timer, or the existing-WFT no-op branch; before releasing the request lease.

UpdaterApplyRequestExisting.trigger: After duplicate object lookup/binding, before unlocked waiting. Capture actual object pointer identity, not just Update ID.

AttachCallbacks.trigger: After the Sent-state callback buffer append; before the requested mutable-state transaction/conversion.

GetUpdateOutcome.trigger: After lookup has returned its event/outcome and constructed the ready result, before API response assembly. Retain actual cache-hit host, five-field key, event Update ID/type/payload, and metadata pointer in the mapped snapshot.

RegistryFindMissing.trigger: After lookup determines missing/closed error, before returning the RPC error.

ScheduleNormalWorkflowTask.trigger: After explicit normal scheduling source constructs WFT/event and transfer mutation; before persistence.

AddWorkflowTaskToMatching.trigger: After Matching accepts AddWorkflowTask and before its History start reentry. Use a test RPC interceptor plus matching-side acceptance marker.

AddWorkflowTaskToMatchingFailed.trigger: After failed direct dispatch is swallowed; delivered distinguishes no Matching acceptance from acceptance with response lost. Establish delivery independently, never infer it from error class.

StickyWorkerUnavailable.trigger: After sticky-unavailable response switches the copied request to the normal task queue; before retry dispatch.

PushWorkflowTask.trigger: After valid durable transfer work is accepted by Matching and transfer eligibility is acknowledged. Read guard snapshot under lease; actual RPC is after lease release.

RecordWorkflowTaskStarted.trigger: After identity validation and mutable start/timer generation; before normal/transient start persistence or speculative response.

CreateRecordWorkflowTaskStartedResponse.trigger: After Registry.Send builds worker response, marking admitted requests Sent, BEFORE normal start persistence. Normal response status is pendingStart until commit; speculative starts may skip persistence. Both use startResponse until successful RecordWorkflowTaskStartedReturn. Inline successors remain pendingResponse until the containing completion RPC returns.

RecordWorkflowTaskStartedReturn.trigger: After setHistoryForRecordWfTaskStartedResp succeeds and the start API returns, outside the Workflow lease. Identify the pending response by its exact task token; only now may the worker use it.

RecordWorkflowTaskStartedNotFound.trigger: After rejecting stale/already-started Matching work without applying it.

WorkerAcceptance.trigger: Worker/test-harness boundary: after appending exactly this acceptance/response/rejection message to the pending completion request, before sending it. Capture actual message order and the worker token associated with that request.

WorkerResponse.trigger: Worker/test-harness boundary: after appending exactly this acceptance/response/rejection message to the pending completion request, before sending it. Capture actual message order and the worker token associated with that request.

WorkerRejection.trigger: Worker/test-harness boundary: after appending exactly this acceptance/response/rejection message to the pending completion request, before sending it. Capture actual message order and the worker token associated with that request.

WorkerSendCompletion.trigger: At worker RPC send: freeze the exact command/message sequence. Use Ignore for a deliberately ignored delivery and Close for a final-close command at the end of the permitted sequence.

WorkerIgnoreUpdates.trigger: At worker RPC send: freeze the exact command/message sequence. Use Ignore for a deliberately ignored delivery and Close for a final-close command at the end of the permitted sequence.

WorkerCloseWorkflow.trigger: At worker RPC send: freeze the exact command/message sequence. Use Ignore for a deliberately ignored delivery and Close for a final-close command at the end of the permitted sequence.

RespondWorkflowTaskCompleted.trigger: Immediately after all task identity guards pass, before AddWorkflowTaskCompletedEvent. Capture BOTH raw token tuple and current WFT tuple for the applied-guard witness.

RespondWorkflowTaskCompletedNotFound.trigger: After identity rejection decides NotFound but before deferred sticky cleanup runs; preserve the current task selected by scheduled ID.

AddWorkflowTaskCompletedEvent.trigger: After deleting current WFT metadata, cancelling its timer, and skipping or materializing WFT events; before Update command processing.

TryResurrect.trigger: After reconstruction from original request carried in acceptance/rejection, before processing that same message. Completion alone cannot trigger this event.

OnAcceptanceMsg.trigger: After acceptance event, buffered callback options events, provisional state, and both effect registrations; before processing the next message. No future is ready merely because this event occurred.

OnResponseMsg.trigger: After provisional completion, completion metadata/cache insertion and effect registration; before persistence. Capture actual event batch pointer from the builder and actual cached event payload.

OnRejectionMsg.trigger: After explicit rejection clears buffered callbacks and registers rejection effects, with no durable rejection event in this scope.

HandleMessageInvalid.trigger: After rejecting a protocol message for its Update state; before error context clearing/cancellation.

HandleCommandsDone.trigger: After remaining messages/final-close command and before RejectUnprocessed/AbortAccepted. Snapshot the actual set of Sent objects eligible for the rejection loop.

RejectUnprocessed.trigger: After EACH iteration of automatic rejection, including the FIRST callback-buffer error that returns from the loop. Do not emit fictitious rejections for the remaining objects.

AbortAccepted.trigger: After EACH provisional abort/effect registration in the final-close batch. Go map iteration order is captured as it occurred.

PrepareWorkflowMutation.trigger: After successor selection and persistence/skip decision; before backend submission or legitimate skip effect Apply.

ConvertSpeculativeWorkflowTaskToNormal.trigger: After conversion materializes scheduled/started events and replaces/cancels timer; before executing the options/update transaction.

UpdateWorkflowExecutionWithNew.trigger: After closeTransaction increments the mutable record version and freezes the execution mutation/tasks, before History append. ctx.rv is the advanced in-memory version; write.rv is the previous expected database version (mutation.DBRecordVersion minus one); db.rv remains unchanged until commit.

AppendHistoryNodes.trigger: After the History append loop completes, before execution transaction submission. Emit the boundary even if the event batch is empty; do not fabricate a physical batch in that case.

ExecutionTransactionCommit.trigger: Immediately after ACTUAL backend commit/applied-CAS, independently of injected timeout result. Capture metadata, record version, committed logical event references and internal tasks atomically. Late settlement needs a backend-side observer/readback.

ExecutionTransactionFenced.trigger: After the real range/version conditional check proves noncommit. Capture expected and actual fence values.

ExecutionTransactionNoncommit.trigger: After a supported definitely-not-committed failure, with backend evidence. Do not classify arbitrary Unavailable/timeout here.

ExecutionTransactionTimeout.trigger: After uncertain execution error is returned and shard lost/reacquisition transition is requested; before Context.Clear. Keep independent DB settlement state.

AppendHistoryTimeout.trigger: After append timeout; execution mutation was not submitted. Retain any physical append actually observed.

HandleWriteResult.trigger: After returned persistence result selects success Apply or deferred Clear-before-Cancel. This marker precedes those separate operations.

BufferApplyFirst.trigger: At EACH callback: after state transition and its FIRST future Set, or after the acceptance deferral branch. Pause point is before the second Set. Capture callback kind, object, prior state, future value/error readiness.

BufferApplySecond.trigger: After the second Set when required and remover; for the no-second-Set branch, after remover/return. Never combine with the first event across a waiter observation.

BufferApplyDone.trigger: After FIFO callback loop and effect/cancel buffer clearing, before post-commit close or response work.

RegistryAbortAfterClose.trigger: Before each immediate post-commit abort callback after normal final closure; use BufferApplyFirst/Second for observable future writes.

AddSuccessorWorkflowTask.trigger: After scheduling speculative successor with bypassTaskGeneration, before inline start; retain the lease.

StartSuccessorWorkflowTask.trigger: After inline speculative start/timer installation, before creating the inline response; retain the lease.

CreateRespondWorkflowTaskCompletedRespon.trigger: After deciding/assembling the successful completion response with no inline successor, before returning it.

RespondWorkflowTaskCompletedReturn.trigger: At successful server RPC return; only here does the inline new WFT become a worker-visible token.

RespondWorkflowTaskCompletedLateError.trigger: At actual injected later-handler failure after persistence/effect publication; before deferred clear. Preserve which response-assembly operation failed.

ContextClearBegin.trigger: After discarding MS/cancelling current speculative pointer; before the registry Abort loop. Host event cache remains intact.

RegistryClearAbort.trigger: Per old registry object, after first outcome Set with registry-cleared error, or after its terminal-state no-op branch.

RegistryClearAbortSecond.trigger: After the preaccepted accepted-future Set in Clear; do not overwrite an already-ready successful accepted future.

ContextClearDone.trigger: After Registry.Clear finishes and registry/context pointers are cleared; old waiter object references remain in the observer table.

BufferCancel.trigger: After EACH rollback callback in reverse registration order, including no-op guards when Context.Clear already aborted the object.

BufferCancelDone.trigger: After LIFO loop and final buffer cleanup/error return.

EvictWorkflowContext.trigger: Controlled workflow-cache eviction trigger outside a held lease; before Clear begins.

LoseShardOwnership.trigger: Controlled shard loss/unload notification at an idle handler boundary; before context clear. Unlike process restart, retain host cache.

AcquireShard.trigger: After a new successful range acquisition and host selection, before MS reload. Capture actual new range, not an inferred increment from an error.

LoadMutableState.trigger: After committed MS and accepted-object registry reconstruction. New object indices use canonical Update order within this unobservable constructor; old waiter indices never change.

ClearStickyTaskQueue.trigger: After Clear/Load, clearing stickiness on reloaded MS; before its real execution-state write.

EvictHostEvent.trigger: On actual entry expiration/eviction/removal, before a subsequent GetEvent can hit it. Record the exact host/key removed.

RestartHistoryHost.trigger: After a detached host process restarts with empty host cache. Active-host loss uses CrashHistoryProcess first.

ScheduleToStartTimerEligible.trigger: When the specific timer becomes due, before scheduler submission. STS means normal fallback eligibility; STC requires actual worker-delay fault. Normal timer eligibility must be backed by committed timer/task state.

StartToCloseTimerEligible.trigger: When the specific timer becomes due, before scheduler submission. STS means normal fallback eligibility; STC requires actual worker-delay fault. Normal timer eligibility must be backed by committed timer/task state.

MemoryScheduledQueueSubmit.trigger: After TrySubmit accepts the eligible noncancelled timer; preserve this bit if cancellation follows.

ExecuteWorkflowTaskTimeoutTaskStale.trigger: After current-state identity/stamp/type-conditional pointer/version/attempt rejection; do not mutate the replacement WFT.

ExecuteWorkflowTaskTimeoutTask.trigger: After validated timeout mutates WFT and schedules its normal/transient successor, before the shared execution transaction. Capture old timer identity, actual current WFT, current pointer and resulting event IDs.

ForceTerminateWorkflow.trigger: When a real configured limit triggers forced termination; before precommit registry abort. Record limit restoration separately.

ForceTerminateAbort.trigger: Before each immediate forced-termination abort callback; BufferApplyFirst/Second record actual future publication BEFORE persistence.

ForceTerminateClear.trigger: After precommit abort loop, immediately before Clear/Load for forced termination.

ForceTerminatePersist.trigger: After terminate mutation (including failing a durable started WFT first), before outer persistence call.

RestoreHistoryLimit.trigger: At explicit test-controller restoration of the runtime History limit; this is part of CR-5 recovery, not an automatic server repair.

TerminateWorkflowExecution.trigger: After external termination mutates state and fails a started WFT first; before transactional persistence and post-success registry abort.

TimeoutWorkflowExecution.trigger: After a valid final Workflow timeout mutates state with no new run; before persistence and post-success abort.

ExternalCloseReturn.trigger: After successful external-close write and all immediate registry aborts, at handler return.

WaitLifecycleStageOutcome.trigger: After waiter obtains/checks the outcome future or decides to inspect acceptance, outside Workflow lease. Use the values returned by the thread-safe Future methods.

WaitLifecycleStageAccepted.trigger: After accepted future Get returns or soft-timeout branch selects ADMITTED; before rechecking outcome for an accepted result.

WaitLifecycleStageOutcomeRecheck.trigger: After the second outcome Ready/Get check, before returning ACCEPTED or COMPLETED to response assembly.

WaitLifecycleStageSoftTimeout.trigger: At actual server soft long-poll expiration. Do not confuse with client deadline or backend timeout.

CreateUpdateResponse.trigger: At actual server response/error return after waiter result assembly; response is now in flight.

ReceiveUpdateResponse.trigger: At CLIENT-side gRPC receipt, after deserialization; record exactly stage and payload/failure/error class. This is the only successful-receipt observation action.

LoseUpdateResponse.trigger: At controlled interceptor dropping an already-produced server Update/Poll response, with proof the server response existed. Client retains a retry path.

RetryUpdateWorkflowExecution.trigger: At retry submission: Update after volatile admission/retryable error, Poll after observed ACCEPTED; preserve Run/Update identity.

ExecutionTransactionBegin.trigger: At submission of the execution mutation to the backend transaction/CAS, separately from eventual settlement and caller return.

CrashHistoryProcess.trigger: At actual process-loss barrier. Cache, volatile timers, effects and server waiters die; already transmitted responses/worker RPCs and submitted backend transactions have separate lifetimes. Record backend settlement independently.

DuplicateWorkerCompletion.trigger: At controlled worker-RPC retry/drop, preserving the original serialized task token and message payload exactly.

LoseWorkerCompletion.trigger: At controlled worker-RPC retry/drop, preserving the original serialized task token and message payload exactly.
